subject: RFP: Commit Shield, Dynamic Overage & Escrow Options
messages:
From: Dana Lee <procure@examplecorp.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP Q: commit shielding and escrow options for commercial appendix

Hi Kimberly / Marissa,

Thanks for the RFP response so far. Our procurement team is working through the commercial appendix and we have a couple of follow-ups specifically around committed volume economics and an escrow/commit-shield idea the business is evaluating. High-level asks:

- Can Redwood provide a short commercial appendix that explains: per-token list price, commit discount tiers, how overage pricing kicks in (per-month vs pro-rata true-up), and any caps you offer during sustained spikes?
- Explain an "escrow" workflow: what does Redwood need to hold committed credit in escrow (mechanics, fees), how are draws billed, and what audit rights do we retain?
- Would Redwood consider a temporary lower escrow fee or rollover window for a first-year contract to help mitigate startup volatility?

We'd like this in a concise doc plus a one-page term stub we can attach to the draft SOW. If you can get us a response and a redlineable stub by EOD Monday (9/6) that would be great.

Thanks,
Dana Lee
Procurement Lead — ExampleCorp
procure@examplecorp.com

[This thread will inform our scoring against the commercial model section of the RFP.]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP Q: commit shielding and escrow options for commercial appendix

Dana —

Appreciate the clear asks. Please find our concise summary below and attached two files: Redwood_Commercial_Appendix_v3.pdf (commercial summary) and Commit_Shield_Terms.docx (term stub you can redline). Key points up front:

- Pricing (hosted inference, generation): $0.0006 per token (list). Commitment discounts by annual committed token baseline: 10% @ >=50M tokens, 18% @ >=200M, 28% @ >=1B. Embedding and reranking have separate tiers (details in appendix).

- Overage mechanics: Monthly true-up by default; usage above committed monthly allocation billed at overage rate = 1.5x list price (can be tiered). For customers that prefer smoothing, we offer quarterly true-up with usage smoothing applied to stay within a rolling quarter baseline.

- Commit Shield / Escrow (mechanics): Customers may elect to place part of their committed spend into an escrow pool administered by Redwood. Escrowed credits: drawn automatically to cover overages during spikes, then reconciled at true-up. Standard escrow fee: 2% of escrowed credit annually (covers administration & short-term capital). Escrow draws are charged at the committed unit price up to the amount available in escrow. Unused escrow balances: available for 30-day rollover; after that they expire unless otherwise agreed. See Commit_Shield_Terms.docx for the template language.

- Dynamic overage cap (optional): For sensitive production workloads we can cap the effective overage price for the first 30 days after a sustained spike (e.g., max 2x committed unit price), after which normal overage rates apply. This is structured as an addendum and requires commit level >= 200M tokens.

- Billing / true-up cadence: Quarterly true-up (default) or monthly on request. Invoices net 30. We support standard procurement data needs: invoice CSVs, per-route token breakdowns, and retention of audit logs for 12 months (longer retention available under Private deployments).

Next steps: I'm looping in Marissa and Rishi internally to confirm whether we can concede on escrow fees and rollover terms for a first-year agreement. We'll come back with a proposed concession and an updated term stub.

Best,

Kim / Marissa —

Quick take (numbers modeled on current cost & forecasted utilization):

- Escrow fee concession: dropping from 2% to 0.5% reduces contribution margin on escrowed balances by ~150 bps (assuming average holding period of 45 days). For a $2M escrow pool that is approx $30k in foregone fee in year one. That's acceptable for strategic customers; recommend approval with a cap: concession valid up to $3M of escrowed credit.

- 60-day rollover: low operational impact; recommend approve for year one only. Make sure term stub states "one-time rollover window; subsequent years follow standard 30-day rollover unless mutually agreed."

- Dynamic overage cap for onboarding: we can include onboarding in the definition but require active monitoring and a one-time request window (customer must notify within first 10 days of production spike). Cap: 2x committed unit price, applies for max 30 days per onboarding event. Require commit >=200M tokens as Kim suggested.

- Escrow custody: strongly prefer Redwood-managed custodial account (operational simplicity). If customer insists on third-party escrow agent, legal & ops will need additional review and possible fees.

If you want, I can draft a short internal approval memo for Sales Ops and Finance to sign off. Otherwise, approved subject to the caps above.

Rishi
Head of Commercial
Redwood Inference

Dana / Marco —

Thanks for the follow-ups. Based on internal review, Redwood is prepared to offer the following commercial concessions for ExampleCorp's RFP (clean and redlineable term stubs attached):

1) Escrow fee: 0.75% for the first 12 months (single-year concession). Applies to Redwood-managed custodial escrow only.
2) Rollover: 60-day rollover on unused escrow balances for the first contract year. After year one, standard 30-day rollover applies unless otherwise negotiated.
3) Dynamic overage cap: Cap of 2x committed unit price for the first 30 days post-production onboarding spike or sustained spike, whichever occurs first. Applies only where commit >= 200M tokens and subject to one-time onboarding notification within the first 10 production days.
4) Billing & true-up: Quarterly true-up by default; monthly true-up available on request. Invoicing net 30. Detailed per-route token CSV and reconciliation report will be provided at true-up.
5) Audit rights: ExampleCorp will receive a reconciliation report and transaction-level pull for true-up periods. For deeper audits, Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II evidence and negotiate reasonable on-site or virtual audit scopes in the contract (subject to NDAs and standard security terms).

Attached: Escrow_Agreement_stub.pdf (redlineable), updated Commit_Shield_Terms.docx (concessions marked), and the commercial appendix in PDF. We have recorded the concession as conditional (max concession exposure $3M escrow pool) — Rishi and Finance flagged this cap.

Next steps: Marco, if you'd like to send a redline to vendor-legal, we'll prioritize a response. If ExampleCorp accepts the concessions, we'll prepare a short addendum to the SOW and schedule a legal sync this week.
